overall: Atlanta is running significantly hotter than expected for June 18, with the observed temperature already reaching 87.8°F by 13:30 ET and still climbing at +3.6°F/hr. The warming trend has been persistent and strong since midday, with skies thinning (FEW coverage) and high dewpoints (~70°F) adding to heat stress. All indicators suggest the daily peak has not yet been reached, with the timing model pointing to a peak near 14:18 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models (ECMWF=81.3°F, HRRR=82.1°F, NBM=81.0°F) are badly underforecasting today — the running max of 87.8°F already exceeds all three model guidance values by roughly 6–7°F. The models also predicted peak timing around 11–12h ET, well before the actual observed peak window, indicating a significant model bust driven by stronger-than-forecast solar heating and cloud clearing.
max_temp_prediction: With 87.8°F already locked in as a running max, a still-positive velocity of +2.7°F/hr (2-hour trend) and roughly 48 minutes remaining before the predicted 14.3h ET peak, the temperature is on track to add approximately 2°F more. The META model concentrates probability in the 88–91°F range (60% combined), with non-trivial upside into 92–95°F (23%). Factoring in the remaining warming window and slightly decelerating acceleration near peak, a best estimate of 90°F seems well-supported, with moderate confidence — the main risk is either a faster cloud-driven cutoff or continued run above 91°F.
